newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CommBank home loan margins easing.
newsitem.headline: CommBank home loan margins easing.

text.p: Commonwealth Bank of Australia managing dirctor David Murray said on Thursday that margins on Australian home loans were now close to international comparisons and any further erosion was likely to be incremental.
"We're either at or fast approaching a margin which is very competitive in world terms for home mortgages," Murray told reporters after addressing a Securities Institute function.
"I therefore believe that the process from here will be incremental."
CBA stunned the home lending market on Wednesday when it cut its key variable home mortgage rate to 7.55 percent from 8.25 percent, its second unilateral rate cut in less than a year.
The bank cut its key variable home loan rate to 9.9 percent from 10.5 percent in May.
That cut triggered a round of mortgage rate cuts by the other major banks and was generally seen as the catalyst to a 50 to 75 basis point cut in big bank home loan margins.

Non-bank lenders like Aussie Home Loans have snared about 10 percent of the market in the last three years with cheap loans funded by securitised bond issues, dragging down home loan margins from about 300 basis points to about 150 points.

Murray earlier told the Securities Institute function that CBA had decided that it had to treat the home loan market like a commoditised product if it wanted to keep and build its presence in banking overall.
"We simply decided (in May last year) that it's a business we intend to be in for the total financial management of our clients affairs and we can only be in it on a commoditised basis," he said.
"I suspect that that means that there'll be a small number of very competitive providers of commoditised home loans," he said.
"There will however be people who have very innovative ways of dealing with clients," he said.

"I don't know how it will all unfold. All I know is that I don't think the Commonwealth Bank can exist with its brand and its scale and its position in the market unless we price according to the reality of the market."
